creator: ryanccooks
title: Smash Burgers
description: Thin, hard-pressed, and cooked in ninety seconds a side. A thick patty is a different and worse sandwich.
steps: Get a heavy pan or flat griddle as hot as it will go. No oil.
Put a ball of mince down and press it flat and thin with a spatula for a full 10 seconds.
Season the top and leave it for 90 seconds, until a dark crust forms and the edges go lacy.
Scrape underneath with the spatula so the crust comes with it, flip, and lay on the cheese.
Cook 60 seconds more, until the beef is cooked through and the cheese has slumped.
Build on the toasted buns with sauce, onion and pickles.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Dry-Brined Baked Wings
description: Baking powder in the rub and a night in the fridge. Crisper than frying and no oil to deal with.
steps: Pat the wings very dry with kitchen paper.
Toss with the baking powder, salt and spices until evenly coated.
Lay them on a rack over a tray and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight, or at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 120C and bake for 30 minutes to render the fat.
Turn the oven up to 220C and bake for 20 minutes more, until deep gold and blistered and cooked through to the bone.
Rest for 5 minutes — they crisp further as they cool.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Reverse-Sear Ribeye
description: Low oven first, screaming pan second. Edge to edge pink with a proper crust.
steps: Salt the steak all over and leave it on a rack at room temperature for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 110C and cook the steak on the rack for 35 minutes, until a probe reads 48C in the centre for medium rare.
Rest it while you get a heavy pan ripping hot with the oil.
Sear for 60 seconds a side, until a hard brown crust forms.
Add the butter, thyme and garlic and baste for 45 seconds.
Rest for 8 minutes before slicing against the grain.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Carolina Pulled Pork
description: Vinegar sauce, not sweet sauce. Six hours in a low oven does what a smoker does, nearly.
steps: Rub the pork all over with the sugar, paprika, salt and pepper. Leave it overnight if you can.
Heat the oven to 135C.
Sit the pork on a rack in a deep tray, add a cup of water to the tray, and cover tightly with foil.
Cook for 5 hours, then uncover and cook for 1 hour more, until the bone pulls clean out.
Rest for 30 minutes, then shred with two forks.
Stir the vinegar and chilli flakes together and pour it over the meat a little at a time until it tastes sharp.
Pile into buns.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Charred Corn Salad
description: Cook the corn until it is genuinely black in places. Half-hearted charring tastes of nothing.
steps: Get a griddle pan or barbecue very hot.
Cook the cobs for 10 minutes, turning, until blackened in patches all over.
Cool for 5 minutes, then stand each cob up and cut the kernels off.
Toss the hot kernels with the mayonnaise, lime, chilli powder and onion.
Fold in the feta and coriander and eat warm.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Beef Brisket Chilli
description: Cubed brisket instead of mince, so it shreds rather than crumbles. No beans, before anyone asks.
steps: Brown the beef hard in the oil, in batches, about 5 minutes a batch. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes, until soft and catching.
Add the garlic and the dry spices and cook for 90 seconds.
Return the beef, add the tomatoes and stock, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 3 hours, until the beef falls apart under a spoon.
Uncover and reduce for 20 minutes, then stir in the vinegar and season.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
description: The brine does the tenderising, the double dredge does the crust. Thermometer, not guesswork.
steps: Mix the buttermilk with the salt and submerge the chicken. Chill for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Season the flour heavily with the garlic powder, paprika and pepper.
Lift each piece out letting the excess drip, dredge in flour, dip back in the buttermilk, then dredge again.
Rest the coated pieces on a rack for 15 minutes so the crust sets.
Heat the oil to 165C in a deep heavy pot.
Fry in batches of three for 14 to 16 minutes, turning once, until deep gold and 74C at the bone.
Drain on a rack, never on paper, and salt straight away.

creator: ryanccooks
title: BBQ Baked Beans
description: Bacon, molasses and two hours. Cook them uncovered for the last half hour or they stay soupy.
steps: Heat the oven to 150C.
Render the bacon in a casserole over medium heat for 6 minutes.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the molasses, tomato purée, mustard and water.
Add the beans, cover, and cook in the oven for 2 hours.
Uncover and cook for 30 minutes more, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Stir in the vinegar at the end to cut the sweetness.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Skillet Cornbread
description: Preheat the pan with the fat in it. The batter should hiss when it hits.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C with a cast-iron skillet inside and the fat in the skillet.
Whisk the dry ingredients in one bowl and the buttermilk, eggs and honey in another.
Combine them with as few strokes as you can — lumps are fine, overmixing is not.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet; it should sizzle at the edges.
Bake for 22 minutes, until the top is golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Turn out after 5 minutes so the bottom does not steam.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Proper Coleslaw
description: Salt the cabbage first and squeeze it. Otherwise you get watery slaw an hour later.
steps: Toss the shredded cabbage with the salt and leave it in a colander for 30 minutes.
Squeeze it hard in your hands, a fistful at a time, to get the water out.
Whisk the mayonnaise, soured cream, vinegar, sugar and celery seed together.
Fold in the cabbage and carrot.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Oven St. Louis Ribs
description: Membrane off, low and slow, finished under the grill. No smoker required.
steps: Slide a knife under the membrane on the bone side and pull it off with kitchen paper.
Rub the racks all over with the sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder and cayenne.
Heat the oven to 135C. Wrap each rack tightly in foil and bake for 2 hours 30 minutes.
Open the foil — the meat should have pulled back from the bone ends.
Brush with sauce and grill on high for 6 minutes, until the glaze bubbles and chars at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut between the bones.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Philly Cheesesteak
description: Freeze the beef for twenty minutes and it slices thin enough. That is most of the recipe.
steps: Freeze the steak for 20 minutes, then slice it as thinly as you can against the grain.
Cook the onion and pepper in half the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, then push them to one side.
Add the rest of the oil and the beef and cook for 3 minutes, chopping it with two spatulas as it browns, until no pink remains.
Mix the vegetables back through and divide into two piles.
Lay the cheese over each pile and let it melt for 1 minute.
Scoop each pile straight into a roll.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Baked Mac and Cheese
description: A real béchamel and two cheeses. The breadcrumb top is not optional.
steps: Heat the oven to 190C.
Cook the macaroni 2 minutes short of the packet time and drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, and cook for 2 minutes without colouring.
Add the warm milk a ladle at a time, whisking, until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon, about 8 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the cheeses and mustard until melted. Do not boil it after the cheese goes in.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish, and scatter with the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and browned on top.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Buffalo Cauliflower
description: Roast it dry first, sauce it after. Battering it before roasting just makes it soggy.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C.
Toss the florets with the oil and salt and spread them out on a tray, cut side down, well spaced.
Roast for 30 minutes, until deeply browned at the edges and tender.
Whisk the hot sauce, melted butter and garlic powder together.
Toss the hot cauliflower through the sauce and return to the oven for 5 minutes.
Serve with the dressing.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Chicken and Waffles
description: Sweet, salty, and a bit much, which is the point. Waffles hold in a low oven.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk for 30 minutes.
Season the flour with the cayenne and plenty of salt, and dredge each tender heavily.
Heat the oil to 175C and fry in batches for 5 minutes, until golden and 74C in the centre.
Drain on a rack and keep warm in a 100C oven.
Cook the waffles until crisp.
Stack chicken on waffle, add butter, and pour the syrup over the lot.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Mustard Potato Salad
description: Dress the potatoes while they are hot so they drink it up. Cold potatoes just get coated.
steps: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and, while still steaming, toss them with the vinegar and a good pinch of salt.
Leave to cool for 20 minutes.
Fold through the mayonnaise, mustard, celery and spring onion.
Add the egg last and turn it through gently.
Chill for an hour before eating.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Grilled Garlic Shrimp Skewers
description: Four minutes total. Overcooked prawns are rubber and there is no coming back.
steps: Toss the prawns with the garlic, oil, lemon zest and paprika. Leave 15 minutes, no longer, or the acid starts cooking them.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over high heat for 2 minutes a side, until pink and opaque all the way through and curled into a loose C.
Squeeze over the lemon and scatter with parsley.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Pimento Cheese
description: Grate the cheese yourself. Pre-grated is coated in starch and it never comes together properly.
steps: Grate the cheese on the coarse side of a box grater.
Mash the mayonnaise, mustard and cayenne together first, then fold in the cheese.
Stir in the peppers and plenty of black pepper.
Leave in the fridge for an hour so it firms up and the flavours settle.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Bourbon Glazed Salmon
description: The glaze reduces to a syrup in the pan. Watch it — it goes from glossy to burnt fast.
steps: Mix the bourbon, sugar, soy and garlic.
Sear the salmon in the oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes on the first side.
Turn, pour in the glaze, and cook for 4 minutes, spooning it over, until the fish is just opaque through the centre and the glaze coats it.
Take the pan off the heat before the glaze darkens past amber.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Banana Pudding
description: Proper custard, not instant. It needs six hours in the fridge before the wafers soften.
steps: Whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour together until pale.
Heat the milk until steaming, then pour it slowly onto the yolks, whisking hard.
Return to the pan and cook over medium-low heat for 6 minutes, stirring constantly, until it thickens enough to hold a line on the back of a spoon.
Stir in the vanilla and press clingfilm onto the surface. Cool completely.
Layer wafers, banana and custard twice in a dish.
Chill for at least 6 hours, then top with the whipped cream.
